services-hub.title: Services Hub
observations: Service hubs work best as navigational pages, not long product-detail pages.
Strong references put service families or self-service choices immediately after a concise hero.
Local Vodafone PNG pages are simpler and category-led; Ooredoo and stc show stronger cross-selling and digital-service depth.
Telikom should expose Personal, Home, Business and Remote/Enterprise pathways quickly while keeping support actions visible.

personal-mobile.title: Personal - Mobile
observations: Plan pages lead with product choice, then make price, data and validity comparison the visual center.
Ooredoo and stc add benefits, roaming and add-ons after the core plan decision instead of before it.
Digicel shows the value of compact tables for dense allowance data, but its support-page presentation is too text-heavy.
Telikom needs a stronger hybrid: scannable plan cards plus a full detail/comparison layer, with USSD activation never hidden.

affordable-home-data.title: Affordable Home Data
observations: Home internet references quickly establish the connection proposition, then move into package comparison.
Ooredoo and stc use benefits and feature blocks to explain why a plan is worth choosing, not just the quota.
Vodafone PNG uses a compact plan table followed by FAQs, which is efficient but visually less persuasive.
Telikom should balance affordability with clarity around supported connection, activation, eligibility and unlimited options.

special-home-passes.title: Special Home Passes
observations: Pass and add-on pages benefit from grouping by intent rather than dumping every offer into one list.
Ooredoo makes promotion cards highly visual; stc gives deeper package detail and terms; Vodafone keeps categories simple.
Time-based or app-specific products must communicate validity windows and usage restrictions before purchase.
Telikom should foreground Video, Night, Study and Weekend use cases and show supported apps directly on the pass card.

u-tokmoa.title: U-TOKMoa Plans
observations: Comparable bundle pages make the package tier or duration choice the primary interaction.
Competitors use benefit blocks to explain bundle value, then defer detailed terms and FAQs.
U-TOKMoa is more voice-specific than most references, so Telikom must make on-net and off-net minutes as prominent as data.
Duration labels should be a first-class selector because daily, weekly, fortnightly and monthly options are central to the product.

home-entertainment.title: Home Entertainment Package
observations: Entertainment pages sell the experience first, then explain package tiers and technology.
Ooredoo separates content ecosystem, TV device and package selection cleanly, which reduces cognitive load.
stc shows the value of integrating entertainment benefits directly into home-connectivity plans.
Telikom should make the triple-play story unmistakable: broadband + TV + fixed voice, with installation and eligibility close to the CTA.

devices.title: Devices
observations: Strong device catalogues put filters, categories and pricing directly beside the product grid.
Verizon and Ooredoo show that dense catalogues need persistent sorting/filtering and clear product cards.
Vodafone PNG product pages are useful local references for merchandising, but one broadband-device capture timed out and is excluded as a reliable structural sample.
Telikom should support phones, MiFi/routers and accessories in one searchable catalogue without burying network compatibility or stock status.

business-fixed.title: Business - Fixed
observations: Business connectivity pages open with outcomes and reliability, then explain the service and enterprise benefits.
stc repeatedly uses package tiers, benefits, add-ons, terms and a lead form in a predictable sequence.
Ooredoo emphasizes benefits and direct sales/support contact earlier, which is useful for high-consideration buyers.
Telikom needs broader solution coverage than any single reference, so category navigation, feasibility and quote tooling are essential.

business-mobile.title: Business - Mobile
observations: Business mobile pages lead with productivity or workforce outcomes, followed by plan tiers.
stc separates package benefits, roaming, service pricing and enquiry forms into distinct decision blocks.
Ooredoo uses strong plan cards and a clear request/contact CTA after the plan decision.
Telikom can differentiate by making CUG/PUG, fleet savings, roaming, SIM management and onboarding part of one coherent business-mobile journey.

news-media.title: News & Media
observations: Newsrooms need a strong featured story plus fast scanning of recent content.
Verizon demonstrates a clear split between editorial stories and formal press releases; Ooredoo adds category filtering.
The 102k-pixel Verizon press-release capture is an over-expanded listing artifact and should not drive layout-length decisions.
Telikom should unify news, notices, promotions, network updates and press material but expose type filters immediately.

about-us.title: About Us
observations: Modern About pages tell a narrative instead of opening with long corporate text.
Telefonica and Verizon use modular story blocks, purpose, impact and innovation to humanize corporate information.
Ooredoo surfaces leadership, vision and CSR as clear visual modules.
Telikom should combine PNG nation-building and infrastructure credibility with leadership, subsidiaries and Foundation/CSR rather than treating them as disconnected records.

store-locator.title: Store Locator
observations: The strongest locator experience is search/map-first, with nearby locations and details synchronized.
Ooredoo combines map pins and a location list cleanly; AT&T prioritizes location search and action buttons.
Digicel and Vodafone PNG show that simple lists or accordions are still useful fallbacks when local map data is incomplete.
Telikom should make PNG region and outlet-type filters first-class and show services, hours, phone and directions without extra navigation.

careers.title: Careers
observations: High-quality careers pages sell the employee proposition before or alongside job search.
AT&T and Ooredoo use career areas, benefits, culture and employee stories to build interest beyond vacancies.
Vodafone PNG is more informational and process-led, while Verizon's capture hit a security verification wall and is not a useful visual reference.
Telikom should keep job search prominent while also explaining PNG impact, culture, benefits and recruitment process.

faqs.title: FAQs
observations: Support hubs put search first, then route users by category or popular issue.
Ooredoo and Digicel combine searchable help with topic tiles; Vodafone's product FAQ shows the value of focused accordion answers.
FAQ pages should not force users to browse everything before reaching support.
Telikom should merge global FAQ search with clear product categories and immediate escalation to contact, store or Self Care when an answer is not enough.

contact.title: Contact
observations: Good contact pages route users by intent or channel before presenting a long form.
Ooredoo surfaces phone, chat and WhatsApp as cards; Verizon organizes support contacts by product line.
Vodafone PNG combines a direct form with a support-hub fallback, which is useful for a smaller market.
Telikom should keep hotline, WhatsApp, email and HQ details visible while separating enquiries, feedback and complaints into explicit paths.
